t.5.42.1: Commanded by the lord of the Rākṣasas, the mighty Jambumālī, son of Prahasta, huge-fanged and bearing a bow, went forth.
t.5.42.2: Wearing red garlands and garments, adorned with a wreath and with splendid earrings, he was huge, with rolling eyes, fierce, and hard to conquer in battle.
t.5.42.4: By the mighty twanging roar of that bow, the cardinal directions, the intermediate quarters, and the sky itself were suddenly filled.
t.5.42.3: Forcefully twanging his great bow, which resembled the bow of Śakra, bore beautiful arrows, and gave forth a sound like the crash of the thunderbolt.
t.5.42.5: Seeing him arrive in a chariot yoked with donkeys, Hanūmān, endowed with great speed, rejoiced and roared aloud.
t.5.42.9: Struck by the arrows of the rākṣasa, the great monkey grew enraged. Then, at his side, he saw a huge and exceedingly broad rock.
t.5.42.11: Seeing that deed come to nothing, the mighty Hanumān of fierce valour uprooted a huge sāla tree and whirled it around.
t.5.42.10: Swiftly tearing it up, the mighty one hurled it with great force; the enraged rākṣasa struck it with ten arrows.
t.5.42.6: The mighty-armed Jambumālī pierced with sharpened arrows that great monkey Hanūmān, who was stationed on the cornice of the archway.
t.5.42.12: Seeing the mighty monkey whirling a sāla tree, the mighty Jambumālī shot a great many arrows at him.
t.5.42.7: He pierced that lord of monkeys in the face with a crescent-headed arrow, in the head with a single barbed arrow, and in the two arms with ten iron shafts.
t.5.42.8: His face, struck by the arrow and turned copper-red, shone like a full-blown lotus in autumn pierced by a ray of the sun.
t.5.42.14: His body filled with arrows and overcome by great fury, he seized that very iron club and swiftly whirled it about.
t.5.42.13: With four arrows he cut apart the sāla tree, and he struck the monkey with five in the arm, with a single arrow in the chest, and with ten between the breasts.
t.5.42.15: Exceedingly swift and mighty in strength, he whirled the iron club with tremendous speed and brought it down upon the broad chest of Jambumālin.
t.5.42.16: Of him there was no head, no arms, no knees; neither bow nor chariot nor horses nor arrows could be seen there.
t.5.42.17: Struck with force by him, that great chariot-warrior Jambumālī fell slain upon the ground, his limbs and ornaments crushed to powder.
t.5.42.18: Hearing that Jambumālin had been slain, and the mighty Kiṃkaras too, Rāvaṇa grew furious, his eyes reddened with rage.
t.5.42.19: When the mighty son of Prahasta had been slain, the lord of the night-rangers, his eyes rolling and copper-red with fury, swiftly commanded the sons of his ministers, men of surpassing valour and prowess.
